title: Georgist land-value taxation and outer-space property law as grounding for NOXIA's land/tax mechanics
question: What does the economic literature on Henry George's land value tax (ground rent, LVT effects on speculation, land-use efficiency and government revenue) establish empirically, and which real outer-space property-law frameworks (Outer Space Treaty Art. II, national resource-extraction legislation, Artemis Accords) constrain or enable private land ownership and 'Grundbücher' on Mars — so that NOXIA's land_value/LVT mechanic, the per-trade colony tax (NOXIA-ECON-0002), the ECO-L1 modules 'Was ist Bodenwert?'/'Was ist Grundrente?' and the draft essay 'Warum der Mars Henry George recht gibt' rest on checked premises rather than asserted ones?
why_now: The colony_admin_tax migration makes land_value a central economic quantity and adds colony tax rates (up to 50%) on trade, while NOXIA-CITY-SIMULATION F2 adopts the Georgist Landwertsteuer as the governance model; the draft Henry George essay is published to players and asserts the Martian colony 'proves' Georgist rent, and the ECO-L1-0002/0003 learning modules teach Bodenwert and Grundrente. The economic evidence for LVT's actual effects and the legal reality of extra-terrestrial property rights are both externally checkable and currently unsourced.
real_world_anchor: Empirical land-value-tax economics (Georgist LVT theory and historical/empirical studies such as the Pittsburgh land-tax experiment) and outer-space property/resource law (Outer Space Treaty Art. II, Commercial Space Launch Competitiveness Act, Artemis Accords) for land ownership and taxation on Mars
